verses.22:1: O Senhor {regit}, e nada me faltará: * num lugar de {pascua}, ali me colocou.
verses.22:3: Guiou-me {semitas}, * por causa do seu nome.
verses.22:4: {pois} no meio da sombra da morte, não temerei males: * porque vós estais comigo.
verses.22:6: E a vossa misericórdia {subsequetur} * todos os dias da minha vida:

decisions.why: The colon says regit, a present of régere. Douay-Rheims has “The Lord ruleth me”; Matos Soares 1932 has “O Senhor me governa”. The LXX ποιμαίνει is both “shepherd” and “rule”; the Hebrew is the noun “my shepherd”. The pasture is the next colon (in loco páscuæ), so this one does not need to say pastor. The glossary’s open row is reger, and the Sunday Sext versicle is this half-verse, so it has to stand alone.

options.label: me rege
options.note: the Latin’s verb; the versicle can open on it

options.label: é o meu pastor
options.note: the Hebrew’s noun, and what the ear expects; the Latin has no pastor here

options.label: me governa
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 — same sense, a commoner verb

options.label: me apascenta
options.note: imports the shepherding of ποιμαίνει into a colon the Latin wrote as regit

decisions.why: páscuæ is genitive singular: a place of pasture, not pastures. Matos Soares 1932 writes the plural “pastos”. The glossary’s open row is pastagem, and the same word has to serve oves páscuæ and pópulus páscuæ ejus. The second half of the verse is also the response of the Sunday Sext versicle, so it opens on the place.

options.label: pastagem
options.note: singular, as the Latin

options.label: pastos
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 — the plural the ear knows

options.label: pasto
options.note: singular, but “lugar de pasto” is a paddock more than a pasture

decisions.why: reféctio is refreshment, restoration — Douay-Rheims “the water of refreshment”; the LXX is ὕδατος ἀναπαύσεως, “water of rest”, which the Latin did not write (that would be réquies). Matos Soares 1932 paraphrases “água fortificante” and turns super into “junto”. The genitive is one of quality (água de refrigério, as água de vida). refrigério is the Church’s word for this and is the glossary’s open row; it is not a common word.

options.label: de refrigério
options.note: the Latin’s noun; quality genitive

options.label: de repouso
options.note: the Greek’s rest, plainer; it is réquies, not reféctio

options.label: que restaura
options.note: a clause for the noun

options.label: do refrigério
options.note: the glossary’s “água do refrigério” — reads as the refreshment’s own water

decisions.why: The perfect in -ávit is ēducāre, “bring up, nourish”, not ēdūcere “lead out” (that perfect is edúxit). Douay-Rheims has “He hath brought me up”; the LXX is ἐξέθρεψέν με, “he nourished me”. Matos Soares 1932 writes “Conduziu-me”, which is the other verb, and the Hebrew’s “he leads me”. The glossary’s open row is nutrir, one family with enutríre.

options.label: nutriu
options.note: ēducāre; the perfect of the chain collocávit … educávit … convértit … dedúxit

options.label: criou
options.note: “reared”; also heard as “created”

options.label: conduziu
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 — ēdūcere, or the Hebrew; the form on the page is educávit

options.label: educou
options.note: the cognate; heard as schooling

decisions.why: The spelling is present or perfect; the verse stands in a run of perfects, the Greek is the aorist ἐπέστρεψεν, and both Douay-Rheims (“he hath converted”) and Matos Soares 1932 (“converteu”) take it as past. D25 keeps voltar for convértere and uses converter where the sense is a soul turned to God (18:8 convértens ánimas). This is that sense. The glossary’s open row already has converteu a minha alma here.

options.label: converteu a minha alma
options.note: D25’s exception, as 18:8

options.label: voltou a minha alma
options.note: the glossary’s ordinary verb; heard as turning the soul around, not as conversion

options.label: fez voltar a minha alma
options.note: the causative the Hebrew שובב can carry; the Latin is the simple verb

decisions.why: sémita is vereda (D15), justítia is justiça, and dedúcere of guidance is guiar (D22). What can still move is super: “sobre as veredas” is the Latin preposition and sounds like walking on top of the paths; “pelas” is how Portuguese says being led along them. Matos Soares 1932 has “por veredas de justiça”, with no article. The noun does not change.

options.note: the path one is led along

options.label: sobre as veredas da justiça
options.note: super kept as sobre

options.label: por veredas de justiça
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 — no article

decisions.why: The Latin has a comma after Nam. Draft 1 kept it. The stylist says the pause at the head of an already long colon makes the voice stumble, and Pois ainda que runs as one unit. The comma is punctuation; nothing else in the colon moves.

decisions.why: The Latin pauses between the rod and the staff. The stylist’s line for this verse drops the comma, and A vossa vara e o vosso cajado is how the pair is said. The two nouns stay.

decisions.why: The only báculus in the psalter, beside virga, which is vara. báculo in Brazil is a bishop’s staff. bordão is a pilgrim’s. cajado is the shepherd’s stick and is a paroxytone, where báculo is a proparoxytone at the mediant. The glossary’s open row is cajado.

decisions.why: virga is feminine and báculus is masculine, so ipsa … consoláta is neuter plural: the two things themselves comforted me. Portuguese puts a mixed pair in the masculine. Draft 1 said eles mesmos. The ambiguity reader heard the rod and the staff; the stylist still found mesmos stiff and pronoun-heavy, and asked for a cleft, which is how Portuguese stresses a subject. That is grammar (D2). The comma after vara goes with the same line.

options.note: draft 2 — the cleft keeps ipsa’s stress

options.label: elas mesmas me consolaram

decisions.why: The open row for in conspéctu is à vista de, and this verse is one of the places it names. “diante de mim” and “perante mim” are what the line is famous as, and they are the words of ante fáciem, which this colon does not have. Douay-Rheims has “before me”; Matos Soares 1932 has “diante de mim”.

options.label: diante de mim

decisions.why: tribuláre stays atribular, one family with tribulátio. The glossary records that readers keep not knowing the verb, and that afligem was asked for and refused because afligir is afflígere’s. advérsus is “against, over against” (LXX ἐξ ἐναντίας; Douay-Rheims “against them that afflict me”). Matos Soares 1932 has “à vista daqueles que me perseguem”, which spends vista and pérsequi’s verb.

decisions.why: impinguáre is “make fat” (pinguis). With in óleo it is the oiling of the head: the LXX is ἐλίπανας ἐν ἐλαίῳ, “you made oily with oil”. Douay-Rheims and Matos Soares 1932 both say “anointed”. engordar is the Latin’s fat and is heard first as making the head stout. ungir is the act, and it shares a verb with úngere, which never stands beside it. untar keeps the grease and stays apart from úngere. The glossary’s open row is ungir.

decisions.latin: calix meus inébrians quam præclárus est
decisions.why: Three words have to stay: cálice, embriagar (the image, not explained), excelente (præclárus). Draft 1 put the cry first so the colon would not close on é, and the stylist named that the worst line: the climax is lost and the colon ends flat on que embriaga. His line is the Latin’s order (cup, then the cry) with the copula before the adjective, so the cadence is excelente, and como for quam, the plainer word (D2). meus stays against the LXX’s “your cup”. The colon is still long.

decisions.why: The only subséqui in the psalter. It is “follow after”, future. The LXX καταδιώξεταί and the Hebrew are “will pursue”, and the Latin did not write pérsequi. Matos Soares 1932 has “irá após de mim”. The glossary’s open row is seguir. ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ is the same colon as 26:4, and it reads the same: todos os dias da minha vida.

decisions.why: ut plus the subjunctive is a purpose clause: the mercy follows so that I may dwell. The Hebrew is “and I shall dwell”, which the Latin did not write. 26:4 has the same words after a request (Uma coisa pedi), and there ut is what was asked, so that psalm says “que eu habite”. Here nothing has been asked; para que is the purpose. The words after the conjunction are 26:4’s: habite na casa do Senhor. domus is casa.

decisions.why: The working phrase is longos dias (20:5, 90:16). in longitúdinem is a duration. Draft 1 said durante to keep the colon within two syllables of the Latin, and Matos Soares 1932 has those words. The stylist found durante heavy at the final cadence and asked for por, which is the glossary’s preposition and the same duration. The shortness (−4) is the cost; durante was there for the counter.

options.label: por longos dias
options.note: draft 2 — the plainer preposition

options.label: durante longos dias
options.note: draft 1 — closer to the Latin’s length; Matos Soares 1932

options.label: em longura de dias
options.note: keeps a noun for longitúdo; longura is not a word one prays

choices.22:1: The two halves are the Sunday Sext versicle and its response, and each has to stand alone. régere stays reger (open row); the pasture is the next colon, so pastor is not smuggled in here. ibi is kept (ali), resumptive, with a comma before it so the place and the placing are two breaths. collocáre → colocar. nihil mihi déerit is future: nada me faltará.
choices.22:2: super kept as sobre (Matos Soares 1932 turns it into junto). educávit is ēducāre, so the Lord nourishes on the water; he does not lead beside it. convértit taken as perfect because collocávit, educávit and dedúxit around it are perfects, and as converter under D25.
choices.22:3: dedúcere of guidance → guiou (D22); sémita → vereda (D15), the plural kept. propter nomen suum → por causa do seu nome, nothing added.
choices.22:4: Nam is pois, not por isso. Draft 2 drops the comma after Pois: the stylist, and the colon is already the length of the Latin. quóniam in the same verse stays porque. ambulávero is a future perfect; ainda que takes the present subjunctive (ande). in médio umbræ mortis stays no meio da sombra da morte. mala stays plural. tu is vós (D1). The ambiguity reader heard males as harms, which is inside the Latin.
choices.22:4b: virga → vara. Draft 2 drops the comma before e and says the comfort as a cleft (foram eles que me consolaram): ipsa’s stress, without mesmos. The pair is still masculine (vara feminine, cajado masculine). The ambiguity reader had heard eles mesmos as the rod and the staff.
choices.22:5: parásti → preparastes. à minha vista stays: the ambiguity reader heard “before me”, and diante is ante’s word. The stylist’s diante is the option. contra stays; em face is the option for the spatial half of advérsus. atribulam stays, though listed as unknown.
choices.22:5b: Draft 2 follows the stylist: the cup first, como é excelente at the end, so the cadence is excelente and not é. The colon is still +4; cálice, embriaga and excelente have no shorter faithful form. The drunken cup is the Latin’s image, not the Hebrew’s overflow. meus stays. Ungistes stays; the latinist’s fartamente is an option.
choices.22:6: subsequétur is future and is follow, not the Greek’s pursue. todos os dias da minha vida copies 26:4. The colon at the end is the Latin’s: the sentence goes on into 22:6b.
choices.22:6b: para que stays: the ambiguity reader heard the purpose. Draft 2 takes por longos dias (glossary, stylist). durante was only holding the syllable count; the colon is now −4, accepted.

audit.note: Drafted from the Latin, the parallels (LXX, Hebrew, Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932) and the glossary. The Diurnal Monástico is not in this worktree (no OCR files), so no cadence was taken from it. Hard readings: regit is not pastor; educávit is nourish, not lead; impinguásti is the oiling, not “make the head fat”; ut inhábitem is purpose, not “I shall dwell”; the cup is meus, not the LXX’s suus. DO’s Portuguese was not used.
Hard pass on draft 1 (ids and marks). One soft flag: 22:5b second colon +4, accepted.
One minor, on 22:5b. Not taken: fartamente is an adverb the Latin does not have. ungistes stays; Engordastes and the latinist’s line are options of impinguasti.

outcomes.remark: impinguasti: ungistes trades the fattening for anointing; fix Ungistes fartamente com óleo a minha cabeça
outcomes.reason: The adverb is not in the Latin. ungistes is the oiling, which he himself calls defensible; the fat is already selectable as Engordastes.

audit.note: Five remarks. Four taken (comma after Pois, the cleft for ipsa, the cup’s order, por longos dias). diante de mim refused: it is ante’s word.

outcomes.remark: comma after Pois stumbles at the head of a long colon
outcomes.reason: Punctuation only.

outcomes.remark: eles mesmos sounds like people; cleft foram eles que me consolaram, and no comma before e
outcomes.reason: A cleft is how the stress of ipsa is said. The ambiguity reader had heard the rod and the staff; the line was still stiff. The comma is decision varaEt.

outcomes.remark: à minha vista is bookish; Preparastes diante de mim uma mesa
outcomes.reason: diante is ante fáciem’s word. à vista is the conspectus row, and the ambiguity reader heard it as before me. His line does not change the order he complains about.

outcomes.remark: the cry before the cup loses the climax; e o meu cálice que embriaga, como é excelente
outcomes.reason: Order, and como is the plainer word for quam. The cadence falls on excelente.

outcomes.remark: durante is heavy at the final; por longos dias
outcomes.reason: The same duration, the plainer preposition, and the glossary’s. durante was holding a syllable count.

audit.note: Sixteen hearings and four unknown words. None moved the ruling. contra’s hostile hearing is already the option em face. refrigério, rege, cajado and atribulam were unknown and stay.

outcomes.remark: me rege: shepherd/guide, or governs; likely governs, the pasture coming later
outcomes.reason: Heard as the Latin’s regit. The shepherd is the next colon. pastor stays an option of regit.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: rege
outcomes.reason: The open row’s verb. He still heard governs. governa is the option.

outcomes.remark: água de refrigério: refreshment, or chilled water; likely refreshment, the word not fully known
outcomes.reason: Heard as refreshment, which is reféctio. repouso and que restaura stay options of refectio.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: refrigério
outcomes.reason: The open row’s noun, and the hearing was still the right one.

outcomes.remark: converteu a minha alma: restored, or religious conversion; likely conversion
outcomes.reason: That hearing is D25’s exception, and Douay-Rheims says converted. voltou stays an option.

outcomes.remark: veredas da justiça: righteousness, or legal justice; likely righteousness
outcomes.reason: Heard as the Latin’s justítia. justiça is the glossary’s word.

outcomes.remark: por causa do seu nome: the Lord’s name, or someone else’s; likely the Lord’s, seu briefly unanchored before vós
outcomes.reason: suum is his. The person-switch is the Latin’s, at 22:4.

outcomes.remark: não temerei males: moral evil, harms, or illnesses; likely harms
outcomes.reason: Harms is inside mala. The illness sense was not the one he heard.

outcomes.remark: sombra da morte: deep darkness, or a shadow death casts; likely mortal danger
outcomes.reason: Heard as the image. The Hebrew’s valley is not in the Latin.

outcomes.remark: a vossa vara: the shepherd’s rod, or a rod of punishment; likely a stick, comfort not obvious
outcomes.reason: vara is virga, and the comfort is the next colon. A rod that can punish is the Latin’s own range.

outcomes.remark: eles mesmos me consolaram: the rod and staff, or some people; likely the rod and staff
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly. The wording still moves, for the stylist’s ear, to the cleft.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: cajado
outcomes.reason: The open row. báculo is the bishop’s staff and a proparoxytone at the mediant.

outcomes.remark: à minha vista: before my eyes, or visible at a distance; likely before me
outcomes.reason: Heard as before me, which is in conspéctu. diante stays an option.

outcomes.remark: contra os que me atribulam: facing them, or a table set as opposition; likely opposition
outcomes.reason: against is in advérsus, and it is Douay-Rheims. The spatial half is already em face, selectable. contra stays.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: atribulam
outcomes.reason: The working verb, one family with tribulação. afligem is afflígere’s and stays an option.

outcomes.remark: cálice que embriaga: abundance and joy, or literal drunkenness; likely drunkenness, and it may sound negative
outcomes.reason: The drunken cup is what inébrians says. Overflow is the Hebrew. The image stays unexplained.

outcomes.remark: quão excelente: how splendid, or a quality judgment; likely how excellent
outcomes.reason: Heard as the exclamation. The colon still moves, for the stylist, to como é excelente after the cup.

outcomes.remark: E para que eu habite: purpose, a wish, or an unfinished sentence; likely the purpose, though E para que sounds unfinished alone
outcomes.reason: Heard as the purpose, which is ut. Read alone, the Latin Et ut is unfinished in the same way: 22:6 ends with a colon.

outcomes.remark: durante longos dias: a long time, or days that last many hours; likely a long time
outcomes.reason: Heard as duration. The preposition still moves to por, for the stylist, not because this was misheard.

outcomes.remark: casa do Senhor: the temple, or heaven; likely either
outcomes.reason: domus Dómini is open in that way. casa is the glossary’s word.

audit.note: v2: comma after Pois dropped; 22:4b cleft and no comma before e; 22:5b cup first, como é excelente; 22:6b por longos dias. ungistes and à minha vista kept. Checks on v2 still pass; soft flags 22:5b +4 and 22:6b −4 accepted in the choices. No critic has read draft 2.
